extracted.intended_audience: authors and peer reviewers preparing or evaluating Registered Reports for the Journal of Child Language
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, submitting, and reviewing Registered Report Protocols (Stage 1) and Registered Reports (Stage 2) for the Journal of Child Language, including required manuscript sections, methodological and analytic pre-registration, data sharing, and reviewer evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports format (definition and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered Reports are a form of empirical article in which the methods and proposed analyses are pre-registered and reviewed prior to research being conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This format is designed to minimize bias in deductive science while allowing exploratory (unregistered) analyses and serendipitous findings. The cornerstone is that a significant part of the manuscript is assessed prior to data collection; acceptance at Stage 1 is an in-principle commitment to publish Stage 2 provided the study follows the pre-registered plan and quality controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial proposal (optional email pre-check)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective authors may submit a brief proposal by email to assess whether their planned study is a good fit for a Registered Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email should contain: (a) brief description of planned study—background, research question, basic proposed methodology (1–2 paragraphs); (b) justification for why a Registered Report is preferred (1–3 sentences), e.g., likely replication value. Editor/Associate Editor may invite Stage 1 submission or recommend traditional route; no commitments at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1: Abstract without results
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 submissions must include a standard abstract but without results and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1: Introduction (full literature review and hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard introduction that reviews relevant literature, motivates the research question, and gives a full description of experimental aims and hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following acceptance, the Introduction should not be altered (except minor stylistic changes at Stage 2 must be marked). Hypotheses cannot be amended or added after Stage 1 acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1: Methods — full description for exact replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a full description of proposed sample characteristics and experimental procedures in sufficient detail to allow another researcher to repeat the methodology exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include criteria for data inclusion/exclusion (e.g., outlier extraction) and objective procedures for defining exclusion due to technical errors, including how and when data would be replaced. Authors are responsible for creating a sufficiently clear narrative including stimulus choice; some materials may be archived in a repository but the methods narrative must allow full evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods addendum (supplemental material for replication details)
rubrics_metrics.description: A methods addendum may contain additional material necessary for exact replication that would be unwieldy in the main text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The addendum will be included as supplemental material. Copies of stimuli may be shared via a data repository (e.g., OSF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical power analysis / Bayesian equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies using standard methods of statistical inference must include a statistical power analysis; Bayesian hypothesis-testing approaches are an encouraged alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated effect sizes should be justified with reference to existing literature where possible. If effect sizes are highly uncertain, variable sample sizes and interim analyses are permissible but must state inspection points in advance, employ appropriate Type I error correction for 'peeking', and outline a final stopping rule. If predicted sample size yields lower power, authors should provide analyses of achievable power and clearly articulate the importance of conducting the study despite lower power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bayesian analysis specification
rubrics_metrics.description: For analyses involving Bayes factors, authors must specify the predictions of the theory to allow Bayes factor calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should indicate what distribution will represent theoretical predictions and how its parameters will be specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit quality control checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit quality control checks are encouraged where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include absence of floor/ceiling effects, positive controls, or other checks orthogonal to the experimental hypotheses. Outcomes of these checks will be considered at Stage 2 to support interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency plans for sequential/follow-up experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: If follow-up experiments rely on outcomes of prior ones, authors must either (Option 1) lay out the specific logic for follow-ups (e.g., flow-chart specifying which experiments under which outcomes) or (Option 2) submit the first experiment as a stand-alone RR and submit subsequent follow-ups as separate Stage 1 RRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed data analysis plan (pre-registered pipeline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a proposed analysis pipeline including all preprocessing steps and precise descriptions of all planned statistical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address type I error inflation from multiple comparisons, list covariates/regressors, specify contingencies for analysis decisions contingent on prior outcomes, include plans for non-convergence of models, and specify any free parameters in advance. The data analysis plan must remain unchanged at Stage 2 unless modifications are approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of planned tables and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly encouraged to specify particular tables and graphs that will be included in the Registered Report (Stage 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These do not need to be included in the published Stage 1 Protocol but help clarify planned analyses and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential results and implications (exhaustive scenario planning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must outline all possible results to the best of their ability and carefully interpret what each would say about the research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dummy graphs for illustration are encouraged. While wording of Results may change between Stage 1 and Stage 2, interpretations must remain consistent with the potential-results section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline for completion of the research and the Stage 2 manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section is not included in the published Stage 1 Protocol, but is required in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviations policy and pre-approval for changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deviation from the stated experimental procedures could lead to rejection of the Stage 2 Registered Report; changes after acceptance due to unforeseen circumstances require consultation with the editor prior to completion of data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor changes may be permitted at editorial discretion and must be reported in the Stage 2 submission. Substantial changes require resubmission as a new Stage 1 Protocol. Registered analyses must be undertaken even when additional unregistered analyses are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2: Raw data and materials sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon Stage 2 submission authors must submit raw data and any digital experimental materials (e.g., stimuli) to a public repository such as OSF, unless prohibited by ethical approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other than pre-registered data, no data acquired prior to acceptance of the Stage 1 Protocol is admissible in the Stage 2 main analyses except in rare cases pre-approved by the Editor. Pilot data or exploratory analyses involving pre-acceptance data must be clearly marked. Raw data must be accompanied by guidance notes to assist replication; analysis scripts and experimental materials should also be uploaded and referenced in the manuscript with DOI links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of data collection timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must collectively certify in the Stage 2 Cover Letter that all non-pilot data were collected after acceptance of the Stage 1 Protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of registered analyses and handling of flawed registered analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome of all registered analyses must be reported in the Stage 2 manuscript unless a registered and approved analysis is subsequently shown to be logically flawed or unfounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such rare cases the analysis should still be mentioned in Methods but may be omitted from Results with justification agreed by authors, reviewers, and editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory (unregistered) analyses reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional analyses not included in the Stage 1 Protocol are admissible but must be clearly justified, methodologically sound, appropriately caveated, and reported in a separate Results section titled 'Exploratory analyses'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid basing conclusions entirely on statistically significant post hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting requirements (NHST)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reporting null hypothesis significance tests are required to report exact p-values and effect sizes for all inferential analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 reviewer criteria: theoretical merit and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should assess whether the question is theoretically important and relevant and whether the study has potential to tell us something interesting about child language; evaluate the logic, rationale, and plausibility of proposed hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 reviewer criteria: literature coverage and writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the introduction does proper justice to existing literature and tells a coherent story, and whether the writing is clear and appropriate to the JCL audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 reviewer criteria: soundness and feasibility of methodology and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the methodology is sound and described in sufficient detail to exactly replicate procedures and analysis pipeline, whether potential sources of bias are described and mitigated, and whether appropriate quality control measures are in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also assess whether analyses are appropriate, whether the study is sufficiently powered, and whether the timeline is reasonable. Keep in mind that acceptance at Stage 1 is an in-principle publication commitment, so methods/analytics must add meaningfully to the literature regardless of outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 reviewer criteria: consistency with Stage 1 and methodological adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: At Stage 2 reviewers appraise whether the Introduction, rationale and stated hypotheses are the same as in the Stage 1 submission and whether authors adhered precisely to the registered experimental procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction and Methods should be identical; minor changes should be clearly marked. Reviewers may be asked to comment on appropriateness of any editorially permitted larger changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 reviewer criteria: quality of Results section
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the Results precisely follow the procedures set out in the detailed data analysis plan and whether analyses are clearly explained in a manner suitable for the JCL audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether any unregistered post hoc analyses are justified, methodologically sound, and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 reviewer criteria: quality of Discussion section
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether interpretation of results is evidence-based, conclusions are justified given the data, and interpretations are consistent with the logic outlined in the Stage 1 'Potential results and implications' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion should be clear, logical, suitable for the JCL audience, critically interpret results in light of existing literature, evaluate discrepancies, and discuss future plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-evaluation on perceived importance/novelty at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions for Registered Reports (Stage 2) should not be based on the perceived importance, novelty or conclusiveness of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may comment on importance or novelty on the record but such comments will not influence editorial decisions. Avoid proposing additional post hoc tests in Stage 2 unless necessary to satisfy Registered Report criteria; suggestions for analyses should generally be made during Stage 1 review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial outcomes and revision process at Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Following peer review of the Stage 1 Protocol, manuscripts may be accepted, offered opportunity to revise, or rejected outright; multiple rounds of review are permitted if progress continues toward acceptable submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Stage 1 Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon successful completion of Stage 1 review and acceptance, the Registered Report Protocol (Stage 1) is published with its own DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows authors to cite their in-progress work and signals the journal's in-principle acceptance to publish the final Registered Report, conditional on adherence to the protocol and quality controls.
